anchors.name: WHO guidance on large multi-modal models
anchors.binding: Ethics and governance guidance from the World Health Organization.
anchors.asks: Lists documenting and summarising patient visits among the uses of large multi-modal models. It warns that automation bias can let errors go unnoticed by health professionals and patients, and asks governments for independent post-release auditing and impact assessment.
anchors.evidence: A count of what the AI tool leaves out, adds or gets wrong on scripted or consented consultations, before rollout and after each update.

anchors.name: EU AI Act Annex I: medical devices
anchors.binding: Law in the EU: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
anchors.asks: AI that is a medical device, or a safety component of one, and needs third-party conformity assessment under the EU's medical device rules becomes high-risk from 2 August 2028 (as amended in July 2026).
anchors.evidence: Measured error counts on your own cases, for your regulatory team to use in its own assessment.

anchors.name: EU AI Act Annex III 5(a) and 5(d)
anchors.binding: Law in the EU: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
anchors.asks: Eligibility for public healthcare services (5(a)) and emergency healthcare patient triage (5(d)) are high-risk uses from 2 December 2027 (as amended in July 2026). Patient-facing chatbots must also tell people they are dealing with AI (Art 50).
anchors.evidence: Measured test results and a failure list on your own cases, before rollout and after each update.
